title: Catholic social teaching and justice
tagline: Dignity, the common good, subsidiarity, solidarity, work, wealth and poverty, migration and creation, explained without taking a party side.
whyItMatters: Catholic social teaching is a body of principles for judging how we live together, not a party platform. Faithful Catholics weigh the same principles and reach different policies, and this course aims to help you do that charitably.

mindset.tip: Ask which principle the person cares about most and start there. Nearly everyone cares about dignity, work or the family.
Separate the principle from the policy. The Church teaches the first firmly; for the second, the Compendium says the faithful may differ (CCC 2420).
Do not use the poor as a debating point. Visit, give and serve; the Fathers do not allow comfort to talk about the poor without helping them (Matthew 25:31-46).
Read the sources yourself before repeating a slogan. Quote the document and its paragraph.
Stay open to the other camp's evidence: markets and state action each have a place in the tradition. Acton and the Catholic Worker are two voices.

resources.title: Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church
resources.creator: Pontifical Council for Justice and Peace
resources.why: The Church's social teaching organised by principle, with the Catechism's paragraphs in view.

resources.title: Rerum Novarum
resources.creator: Pope Leo XIII
resources.why: The founding document of modern Catholic social teaching, on labour, wages and property.

resources.title: Quadragesimo Anno
resources.creator: Pope Pius XI
resources.why: Where the principle of subsidiarity is named most clearly.

resources.title: Laborem Exercens
resources.creator: Pope John Paul II
resources.why: On work as a way of taking part in creation and as a basis of dignity.

resources.title: Centesimus Annus
resources.creator: Pope John Paul II
resources.why: After 1989: a weighing of markets, socialism and the role of the state.

resources.title: Caritas in Veritate
resources.creator: Pope Benedict XVI
resources.why: Love joined to truth as the basis for economics and politics, with a stress on gratuitousness.

resources.title: Laudato Si'
resources.creator: Pope Francis
resources.why: The Church's teaching on care for creation and the link between the earth and the poor.

resources.title: Dilexi Te
resources.creator: Pope Leo XIV
resources.why: Leo XIV's 2025 exhortation on love for the poor, drawing on the Fathers and the saints.

resources.title: Seven Themes of Catholic Social Teaching
resources.creator: U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops
resources.why: One page that lists the seven themes with short descriptions.

resources.title: CST 101
resources.creator: Catholic Relief Services
resources.why: Short free lessons for groups and individuals on the main principles.

resources.title: Strangers No Longer: Together on the Journey of Hope
resources.creator: U.S. and Mexican bishops
resources.why: The bishops' joint pastoral letter on migration, balancing welcome and the rights of nations.

resources.title: Acton Institute
resources.creator: Acton Institute
resources.why: A Catholic-founded think tank arguing that free markets and human dignity belong together.
resources.note: Takes a market-friendly view; useful as one reading of the tradition, not the only one

resources.title: Catholic Worker Movement
resources.creator: The Catholic Worker Movement
resources.why: Dorothy Day's movement of hospitality, voluntary poverty and nonviolence.
resources.note: Reflects a more radical reading of the tradition

resources.title: What's Wrong with the World
resources.creator: G. K. Chesterton
resources.why: Chesterton's witty case for the family, small property and ordinary people.

resources.title: Who is the Rich Man That Shall Be Saved?
resources.creator: Clement of Alexandria
resources.why: An early Christian homily that says wealth is not condemned but must be used well.

resources.title: Homily 50 on Matthew
resources.creator: John Chrysostom
resources.why: Chrysostom presses the claim of the poor on the comfortable.
